findings.title: Send GitLab an email, push to main
findings.summary_md: Original researcher disclosure by Joe Leon of Aikido Security, published September 23, 2026 (RSS pubDate Wed, 23 Sep 2026 06:00:00 GMT), roughly a day before the story's first_seen. Details the account-scoped, non-expiring glimt- incoming email token, the -issue to -merge-request suffix swap with a git .patch attachment, the IP-restriction bypass demonstrated against a private project, and the nine token permissions including repository update and protected branch update. Reports GitLab closed the May 2026 HackerOne submission as intended behavior, and that Aikido found a dozen live incoming addresses published in public documentation.

findings.title: Merge request !247431: Align incoming email token capability across UI and docs
findings.summary_md: GitLab's shipped response to the incoming email token issue, opened July 28, 2026 and merged August 10, 2026 into milestone 19.3. Changes are copy-only: it removed the claim that the token cannot access any other data, added 'and merge requests' to the UI modal and token description, and documented that incoming email is not subject to IP restrictions. The underlying mechanism was left unchanged.

findings.title: Work item #617883: Email verification for incoming email token actions
findings.summary_md: Open GitLab feature issue, created August 19, 2026, proposing that incoming email token actions be accepted only from a verified email address tied to the token owner's account. Still in New state and unassigned, targeted at milestone 19.5 due October 9, 2026; GitLab maintainers noted that enabling it by default could be a breaking change for forwarded-mail and automation use cases.
